answer: A vote is a reserved deposit, not a username. Each identity funds its own vault with a published bond and a unique ivory serial stamped at intake. Withdrawal stays blocked through a canyon of one epoch plus three delayed peer audits that re-read the serial under a fresh nonce. If two identities share a serial, or an audit finds it was transferred, the bond burns and both votes are void. A farm of a hundred aliases must lock a hundred bonds and wait out a hundred audit paths; serial collisions expose shared capital, so splitting names cannot multiply influence.
